stories.title: SEBI increases oversight for independent directors
stories.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is tightening corporate governance rules for listed companies. The regulator emphasized that board accountability requires more than statutory compliance, calling for independent judgement and transparent decision-making. Independent directors are now expected to look beyond their basic eligibility requirements.

stories.title: Elentec Discloses First Sustainability Report - TipRanks
IperionX Publishes Fifth Annual Sustainability Report Covering Fiscal Year 2026 Operations - Kalkine
Signature Flooring publishes second sustainability report
stories.summary: Signature Flooring has released its second annual sustainability report, titled Sustainability Crafted Into Every Space. The company says the document highlights progress in environmental stewardship and responsible manufacturing. It aims to measure environmental impact and support healthier spaces through its evolving sustainability strategy.

stories.title: Kayseri Şeker Submits TSRS-Compliant Sustainability Report - TipRanks
Sofidel prepares sustainability statement under new EU framework
stories.summary: The Sofidel Group has prepared its latest sustainability statement while aligning with the European Sustainability Reporting Standards. The company noted that the document was produced despite a two-year deferral of mandatory application for the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive and an ongoing review of the reporting framework.

stories.title: Guardian Media Group reports emissions progress
stories.summary: Guardian Media Group has published its 2025/26 sustainability report, stating that emissions are down 8 percent on last year and 52 percent against its 2020 baseline. The company says it remains on track to meet its 2030 target, as reported by its own press office.

stories.title: Richmond Football Club releases 2026 impact report
stories.summary: Richmond Football Club has released its 2026 impact and sustainability report. The club says it remains committed to creating positive change beyond the game. The report highlights initiatives across Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander leadership, aiming to make a contribution to people, communities and the environment.

stories.title: Dustin’s Annual and Sustainability Report Covers 2025/26 - TipRanks
Deloitte finds sustainability reporting challenges persist
stories.summary: A Deloitte study of Central European companies found that only 7 percent of firms disclosed quantitative data on the financial effects of sustainability risks. Only 4 percent quantified anticipated financial impacts. Connecting sustainability disclosures to financial results remains the primary challenge in the second year of reporting.

stories.title: Investment managers seek usable sustainability data
stories.summary: Investment managers are navigating a complex regulatory landscape as they attempt to collect and compare sustainability information. The challenge for firms operating across the UK and EU is not the volume of information disclosed, but whether that data can be reliably used to meet their own obligations.

stories.title: EU sets carbon cost deduction rules for CBAM
stories.summary: The European Commission has established rules for deducting carbon prices paid in non-EU countries from importer obligations under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. Turkey’s Emissions Trading System is now explicitly recognized alongside systems in China, India, South Korea and the United Kingdom.

stories.title: MMCM and CerCarbono issue vehicle scrapping carbon credits
stories.summary: Meta Materials Circular Markets has announced the issuance of 24,988 carbon credits from vehicle material recovery. The project covers 20 scrapping facilities across India. The company describes the initiative as a milestone for circularity-linked carbon finance and a new revenue opportunity for the vehicle scrapping industry.

stories.title: Climate finance negotiations stall at COP31
stories.summary: Negotiations at COP31 in Turkey remain deadlocked with 21 agenda items awaiting agreement. Ministers have called for more targeted support to help developing countries implement climate commitments. Representatives highlighted a persistent gap between national climate targets and the resources currently available to implement them.

stories.title: Honourable Member of Parliament Kamal Subedi's closing remarks at the COP31 side event - From Carbon Registry to Green F
Uganda launches national carbon project register
stories.summary: Uganda has launched a digital register to track carbon projects and transactions. Developed with the East African Carbon Company, the platform aims to improve transparency by recording projects from initial approval through to credit retirement. The government says the move will strengthen oversight of the carbon market.

stories.title: Indonesia announces mangrove carbon projects
stories.summary: Indonesia has unveiled three mangrove and seagrass carbon projects at COP31. While the government aims to position the country as a supplier of nature-based offsets, none of the announced projects have yet produced a tradeable credit. The credits remain in the planning phase.

stories.title: Nepal seeks carbon market investment
stories.summary: Nepal is working to turn institutional preparations into actual carbon credit transactions. During a discussion at COP31, officials explored ways to attract international investment through the country's National Carbon Registry. The government is currently seeking to expand cooperation with international buyers and development partners.

stories.title: Multilateral banks could unlock climate financing
stories.summary: NK Singh, chairman of the 15th Finance Commission, stated that multilateral development banks could unlock billions in lending capacity to boost global climate financing. Singh identified climate finance, renewable energy transitions and carbon market development as the three primary priorities for global climate action at COP31.

stories.title: Ghana receives first African forest carbon credits
stories.summary: Ghana has received 6.57 million carbon credits under the Architecture for REDD+ Transactions, becoming the first African nation to do so. The government expects to generate US$43 million from the sale of these credits, which cover forest protection efforts spanning 2.5 million hectares between 2017 and 2021.

stories.title: EU formalizes 25 million euro loss and damage pledge
stories.summary: The European Commission has signed a 25 million euro contribution agreement with the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage. The deal, signed at the COP31 summit in Türkiye, formalizes a pledge made at COP28. The board expects to approve its first funding decisions this December.

stories.title: Green bond issuance grows 29 percent
stories.summary: Global green bond issuance reached 188 billion dollars in the third quarter of 2026, a 29 percent increase over the same period last year. According to Moody’s, labelled sustainable bond volumes are currently on pace to reach a multi-year high, totaling 878 billion dollars year-to-date.

stories.title: Philippines joins carbon trade coalition
stories.summary: The Philippines has joined an 18-country coalition aiming to expand high-integrity carbon credit markets. Environment Secretary Juan Miguel T. Cuna announced the country would endorse the Antalya Statement to help mobilize private climate financing and support the development of a national carbon market.

stories.title: Oil Change International COP31 Media Advisory to November 19, 2026 - Oil Change International
Mary Robinson at COP31: ‘We’re all dandelions together’ - Sustainable Views
COP31 negotiators face unresolved agenda items
stories.summary: With two days remaining at COP31, the summit presidency has urged parties to accelerate progress as 21 mandated items remain unresolved. Negotiators are currently deadlocked over fossil fuel transition plans, electrification pledges and strategies to address temperature overshoot beyond the 1.5C Paris Agreement targets.

stories.title: Fossil fuel lobbyists attend COP31
stories.summary: One hundred corporations and industry groups with fossil fuel ties, including ExxonMobil and TotalEnergies, have sent delegations to the COP31 climate summit. This follows the attendance of more than 1,700 lobbyists at the 2024 talks in Azerbaijan and over 1,600 at the 2025 summit in Brazil.

stories.title: COP31: Vanuatu calls for UN climate summit reform, warns of backsliding - France 24
Oil interests and climate diplomacy collide
stories.summary: As COP31 nears its conclusion, delegates remain divided over fossil fuel ties and climate finance. While supporters argue the summit process is essential, critics describe the event as a greenwashed circus. The summit continues to face accusations of diplomatic gridlock regarding its core climate objectives.

stories.title: Diplomats report politicized attack on climate research
stories.summary: Laurence Tubiana, a veteran French climate diplomat, stated that the science informing COP31 is under a serious and highly politicized attack. She identified Russia, Saudi Arabia and India as the three nations responsible for the current stalemate regarding research funding and climate assessment strategies.

stories.title: Countries launch climate progress check at COP31
stories.summary: Countries at COP31 have launched a second five-yearly check of collective progress under the Paris Agreement. Ministers remain deadlocked over the summit's primary questions, including the funding of climate action and the speed of the global transition away from fossil fuels as the deadline approaches.

stories.title: ‘Shocking’ Signs of Climate Change Add Urgency to COP31 Talks - The New York Times
Panama minister criticizes fossil fuel influence
stories.summary: Panama’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, stated the world is being held hostage by the petroleum mafia. As the COP31 summit concludes, 30 countries have signed on to forge a new fossil fuel treaty separate from the official UN process to address the ongoing deadlock.

stories.title: Norway minister notes COP31 negotiation hurdles
stories.summary: Norway’s Climate and Environment Minister Sigrun Aasland stated that COP31 negotiations face multiple difficult issues. Aasland emphasized the urgency of limiting temperature overshoot and advancing the energy transition, noting that she expects the final outcome to include language regarding renewable energy and electrification.

stories.title: Countries air grievances in search of COP31 climate deal - France 24
Pandrol receives circular economy award
stories.summary: Rail infrastructure specialist Pandrol has received an award from SNCF for its commitment to the circular economy. The recognition, presented at the SNCF Group Supplier Awards, honors the company’s efforts to keep materials in use and reduce carbon emissions within railway track maintenance and projects.

stories.title: Otto Cannon advocates for circular economy at COP31
stories.summary: Otto Cannon has called for a global shift from conventional waste management to a circular economy at the COP31 climate conference. He urged countries to prioritise waste reduction, reuse and recycling. The ambassador noted that while waste generation is inevitable, the current methods of disposal require significant improvement.

stories.title: Closed Loop Partners details circular economy strategy
stories.summary: For the last 14 years, Ron Gonen and his team at Closed Loop Partners have focused on building resilient local supply chains. The firm operates through a combination of private equity, venture capital and innovation centres to identify and scale infrastructure that supports the circular economy.

stories.title: Circularity Gap Report highlights global waste
stories.summary: The Circularity Gap Report 2026 found that only 7.2% of materials are cycled back into the economy, leaving 31% of global GDP lost to waste. Closing this gap requires redesigning how products are engineered and repaired at industrial scale. Leadership is measured by influence across entire value chains.

stories.title: Irish minister calls for circular economy mindset shift
stories.summary: Minister James Lawless says Ireland needs a shift in mindset regarding the circular economy. Speaking at a facility that has refurbished 500,000 ICT devices, he highlighted the technical processes required to return discarded electronics to circulation. The facility manages everything from data erasure to cosmetic re-skinning of hardware.

stories.title: Pokhara hosts festival for waste management
stories.summary: The RU Fest has launched in Pokhara to promote sustainable waste management and green job creation. Organised with the help of international agencies, the festival aims to change the perception of waste. Local officials emphasised that discarded materials should be viewed as an economic and social opportunity.

stories.title: UNDP and NPAP discuss plastics treaty in Ghana
stories.summary: The UNDP and Ghana National Plastic Action Partnership have held a dialogue on the country's preparations for a global plastics treaty. The project, funded by a 7 million dollar grant from the Global Environment Facility, aims to establish a framework for the plastics sector in Ghana.

stories.title: Malaysia eyes sewerage sector for circular economy
stories.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Fadillah Yusof says the sewerage sector could drive a national circular economy through biogas energy and biosolid fertilisers. The government is also exploring the resupply of treated water to data centres. The nation is currently using products derived from sewage biosolids to support sustainability.

stories.title: Recove Ventures raises Rs 56.25 crore
stories.summary: B2B circular economy startup Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore in a funding round consisting of equity and debt. The company plans to use the capital to expand its plastic recycling infrastructure in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Existing backers and new investors participated in the round.

stories.title: COP31 urged to address plastic production emissions
stories.summary: The Environmental Justice Foundation is calling on world leaders at COP31 to reduce plastic production. The group notes that plastic emissions currently exceed two billion tonnes of CO2e annually and are set to double by 2060. The climate impact of plastic is described as hiding in plain sight.

stories.title: Recove Ventures secures funding for recycling infrastructure
stories.summary: Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore to build supply chain infrastructure for India’s plastic recycling industry. The funding includes Rs 36.25 crore in equity and Rs 20 crore in debt. Investors include Samara Capital and several family offices. The capital is earmarked for new circular economy infrastructure.

stories.title: Fearnley-Whittingstall criticises circular economy plan delay
stories.summary: Chef Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall has joined campaigners to demand the publication of England's Circular Economy Growth Plan. The government originally committed to launching the strategy in 2025 following input from an independent taskforce. The plan remains unpublished despite the government's previous commitment to prioritise reuse and repair.

stories.title: Gentari expands renewable platform with KKR investment
stories.summary: Gentari has partnered with KKR to expand its renewable energy business in India. KKR made a minority investment in the company's local subsidiary to provide growth capital. Gentari’s platform currently has approximately 8 GW of renewable energy capacity, supported by rising demand and favourable market conditions in India.

stories.title: KKR takes minority stake in PETRONAS’s renewable energy business in India - Traders Union
Indika Energy exceeds 2030 renewable target
stories.summary: Indika Energy reduced its Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 31.44% in the first nine months of 2026. Renewable energy now accounts for 40.40% of the company's total consumption, exceeding its 2030 target. The firm is on track to meet its goal of a 33% emissions reduction.

stories.title: Amazon commits $7 billion to Indian renewables
stories.summary: Amazon plans to invest 7 billion dollars in Indian renewable energy projects by 2030, adding to 4 billion dollars already contracted. The company also announced four new wind and solar projects totalling 934 MW. Amazon aims to cut the carbon intensity of its electricity by 65% by 2030.

stories.title: Google signs deal for superhot geothermal power
stories.summary: Google has signed a power purchase agreement to buy 50 MW of superhot geothermal power from Quaise Energy. The power will be sourced from Project Obsidian in Oregon starting as early as 2030. The project is expected to create hundreds of construction jobs and support Google's data centres.

stories.title: Nvidia reports record revenue amid leadership change
stories.summary: Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, more than doubling its sales from the previous year. The results follow the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang on November 12. The board confirmed it does not intend to reinstate him as the company manages rising AI emissions.

stories.title: Amazon invests 6.3 billion euros in Indian renewable energy
stories.summary: Amazon will invest 6.3 billion euros in Indian renewable energy projects to power its data centres. The funding supports India's goal of 500 gigawatts of clean energy capacity by 2030. Coal and oil remain central to the country's current energy mix. The grid is still catching up.

stories.title: Jakson Green to acquire majority stake in Ocior Energy
stories.summary: Jakson Green has signed agreements to acquire a majority stake in Ocior Energy. The deal combines Ocior's green hydrogen and ammonia development pipeline with Jakson Green's existing renewable energy infrastructure. The acquisition spans projects across India, the Middle East and North Africa.

stories.title: Sunsure Energy to supply 434 MW of power to Amazon
stories.summary: Sunsure Energy has signed a power purchase agreement to supply 434 MW of wind and hybrid energy to Amazon from two projects in Karnataka. The company expects to commission the facilities by late 2027. The wind and solar sectors continue to add capacity to the grid.

research.summary: As India embarks on its first manned space mission, developing indigenous capabilities in crew selection and training not only lays the foundation for sustained space activities but also gives an impetus to bioastronautics, the study of behavioural, and medical aspects of humans living in space

research.title: How do autistic people parse information? A video game can help say
research.summary: Researchers have developed a non-verbal online game that adolescents across the autism spectrum can learn and play, it holds special promise for India by bypassing the need to translate complex clinical instructions into regional languages and allowing clinicians to reach autistic individuals far beyond the major metros

research.summary: The Andaman cobra is highly venomous, and on top of that is capable of spitting venom as a defence mechanism, raising the probability of people killing it out of fear
